title: Two NLIP messages in one CBOR frame

source.clause: §7.1 ("shall contain a single NLIP message encoded in CBOR")
source.note: composed: the encodings of `{"format":"text","subformat":"english","content":"first"}` and of the same message with `second`, concatenated. Each half is conformance/tools/cbor_encode.py output; the frame is the two halves joined, with nothing between them.

notes: A CBOR reader stops at the end of the first item, so an implementation that never looks at the remainder decodes this as `first` and silently loses `second` — which is why the case exists. The JSON wire needs no counterpart: a JSON parser already refuses trailing characters, and §7.1's "a single NLIP message" is what makes the two wires answer alike. The kind is `cbor` because what is wrong is the frame, not the message inside it.
